## Introduction
This document contains the data engineering required to reconstruct and improve the plot shown in Figure 1, visualizing the resale flat prices in Singapore by planning area from 2017 to 2020. The heat map displays the spatial distribution of resale prices, with color intensity representing different price ranges. Blue hues indicate lower prices, while red hues indicate higher prices. This visualization aids in identifying areas with varying resale flat values, providing insights into the property market across Singapore.

The code below requires the following packages:
```{r}
#| label: required-packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

packages = c('sf', 
             'tmap', 
             'tidyverse', 
             'cartogram',
             'ggplot2',
             'dplyr',
             'repr',
             'viridis',
             'RColorBrewer',
             'knitr')

for (p in packages){
  if(!require(p, character.only = TRUE)){
    install.packages(p)
  }
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-original
#| fig-cap: "Geographical Price Heatmap of Resale Flats.The dataset used contain information on all resale HDB flat transactions from 2017 to 2020"
#| out-width: 100%
#| echo: false

include_graphics("images/original.png")
```

## Data Cleaning
The visualization is based on resale flat price data and a shapefile representing the planning areas in Singapore. The data includes:

1. Geospatial shapefile for planning areas

2. CSV file containing resale flat prices from Jan 2017 to May 2024

The CSV file will be trimmed to show only the past 3 years worth of data from Jun 2021 to May 2024. Limiting the dataset to the past three years ensures that the visualization reflects current market trends and conditions. Older data may not accurately represent the current state of the real estate market, as economic conditions, government policies, and buyer preferences can change over time.
```{r}
# Read CSV data
csv_data_path <- "flatprice5.csv"
data <- read.csv(csv_data_path)
filtered_data <- subset(data, month >= "2021-06" & month <= "2024-05")
row.names(filtered_data) <- NULL

# Check if 'town' column exists and rename it to match shapefile
if ("town" %in% names(filtered_data)) {
  filtered_data <- filtered_data %>%
    rename(PLN_AREA_N = town)
} else {
  stop("The column 'town' does not exist in the CSV data.")
}

# Summarize the data to get average resale price for each town
data_summary <- filtered_data %>%
  group_by(PLN_AREA_N) %>%
  summarise(avg_resale_price = mean(resale_price, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## Load and Process shapefile
```{r}
#| message: false
#| output: false

# Read and process shapefile
shapefile_path <- "data/geospatial/MP14_PLNG_AREA_NO_SEA_PL.shp"
singapore_map <- st_read(shapefile_path)
singapore_map$geometry <- st_make_valid(singapore_map$geometry)
singapore_map <- singapore_map |>
  mutate(PLN_AREA_N = ifelse(grepl("Islands|Catchment", PLN_AREA_N, ignore.case = TRUE), "", PLN_AREA_N))


# Ensure 'PLN_AREA_N' exists in both data frames before merging
if (!"PLN_AREA_N" %in% names(singapore_map)) {
  stop("The column 'PLN_AREA_N' does not exist in the shapefile data.")
}

# Merge the summarized data with the shapefile data
singapore_map <- singapore_map %>%
  left_join(data_summary, by = "PLN_AREA_N")

# Check if the merge was successful
if (nrow(singapore_map) == 0) {
  stop("The merge resulted in an empty data frame. Please check the input data.")
}

# Check for NA values in 'PLN_AREA_N'
print(sum(is.na(singapore_map$PLN_AREA_N)))

# Verify merged data
print(head(singapore_map))
str(singapore_map)
```



## Choropleth
The choropleth map visually represents average resale prices of flats across different planning areas in Singapore. This type of map uses color gradients to indicate variations in data across geographical regions.
```{r}
#| message: false

# Set the tmap mode
tmap_mode("plot")

# Plot the map with labels
singapore_map_plot <- tm_shape(singapore_map) +
  tm_polygons(col = "avg_resale_price", palette = "Blues", title = "Avg Resale Price") +
  tm_text("PLN_AREA_N", size = 0.5, col = "black", shadow = TRUE, root = 4) +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Map of Singapore Planning Areas", main.title.position = "center")

# Print the map object
print(singapore_map_plot)
```

## Cartogram
A cartogram distorts the geographical boundaries of regions based on a variable of interest (here, average resale prices). This technique provides a visual representation where the size of each planning area is adjusted relative to its resale price.

By removing excessive town names and focusing on the most relevant ones correlated with resale values, the cartogram visualization becomes a more effective tool for conveying spatial patterns and trends in Singapore's housing market. It strikes a balance between providing detailed information and maintaining visual clarity, ultimately enhancing the viewer's ability to interpret and derive insights from the data.
```{r}
#| message: false

# Fill NA values in avg_resale_price with a default value (50,000)
singapore_map$avg_resale_price[is.na(singapore_map$avg_resale_price)] <- 50000

# Create a new column for labeling based on avg_resale_price
singapore_map <- singapore_map %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(avg_resale_price < 450000 | avg_resale_price == 50000, NA, PLN_AREA_N))

# Create the cartogram
singapore_cartogram <- cartogram_cont(singapore_map, "avg_resale_price", itermax = 10)

# Set the tmap mode
tmap_mode("plot")

# Define the breaks and labels for the color scale
breaks <- c(50000, 450000, 500000, 550000, 600000, 650000, 700000, 750000, 800000)
labels <- c("Missing" , "450,000 to 500,000", "500,000 to 550,000", "550,000 to 600,000", "600,000 to 650,000", "650,000 to 700,000", "700,000 to 750,000", "750,000 to 800,000")

# Create a factor column for avg_resale_price with specified levels
singapore_map$avg_resale_price <- factor(singapore_map$avg_resale_price, levels = breaks)

# Define your color palette and breaks
palette <- c("grey", brewer.pal(5, "Blues"))  # Replace '5' with the number of colors you need

# Plot the cartogram with custom colors
singapore_cartogram_plot <- tm_shape(singapore_cartogram) +
  tm_polygons(col = "avg_resale_price", palette = palette, title = "Avg Resale Price", breaks = breaks, labels = labels, colorNA = "grey") +
  tm_text("label", size = 0.5, col = "black", shadow = FALSE, root = 4) +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Cartogram of Singapore Planning Areas", main.title.position = "center")

# Print the map object
print(singapore_cartogram_plot)
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false

# Saving the generated cartogram as a png
tmap_save(singapore_cartogram_plot, filename = "images/cartogram.png")
```
